# notavibe

> Ranks open-source npm projects on maintenance, not popularity. Five sourced
> signals per project — release cadence, response time, contributor breadth,
> security posture, and adoption — each shown as a named band with its data
> source and fetch date. No composite score. Exposed as an MCP server so coding
> assistants can ground dependency recommendations in real data.

## Site

- [Home](https://notavibe.dev/): what notavibe measures, the five signals, and how to connect the MCP server
- [Privacy policy](https://notavibe.dev/privacy/): what personal data the site handles, why, who processes it, and GDPR rights

## Sections on the home page

- [Five signals, fully sourced, no black box](https://notavibe.dev/#how-it-works): the five maintenance signals and why each is reported as a band with its source and fetch date rather than a score
- [Connect the MCP server](https://notavibe.dev/#install): a hosted remote MCP server at `https://notavibe.dev/mcp` (streamable HTTP, no API key); set up by URL, with a Claude Code command, or with a JSON config
- [Built for the questions your tooling doesn't answer](https://notavibe.dev/#why): what notavibe is for, and what it deliberately is not

## Reference

- MCP server: `https://notavibe.dev/mcp` (HTTP). Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http notavibe https://notavibe.dev/mcp`
- MCP tools (all read-only): `search_projects`, `get_project`, `compare_projects`, `get_lists`

## Notes for agents

- notavibe reports maintenance signals, not security vulnerabilities. It is not a CVE scanner.
- Every signal is a named band carrying its own source and fetch date. There is no single composite score, and inventing one misrepresents the product.
- "Insufficient data" is a valid answer and is reported as such rather than guessed.
- The catalog currently covers one ecosystem: JavaScript and TypeScript.
